newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto to visit Burma, Laos, Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto to visit Burma, Laos, Cambodia.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto will visit Burma, Laos and Cambodia next month in a tour of the three future ASEAN members, official sources said on Saturday.
"There is a plan not only to visit Myanmar (Burma) but also Laos and Cambodia," the Indonesian official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The trip was scheduled for the third week of February, although its exact timing had not yet been finalised, the official said.
Suharto would probably spend two or three days in each country as is usual on state visits, the official said.
"He hasn't been in that region for some time," the official added. There were no further details available.
In November, the leaders of the three countries visited Indonesia to take part in the Association of Southeast Nations (ASEAN) informal leaders summit.

The ASEAN summit ended with a declaration that the seven member grouping would simultaneously admit Burma, Laos and Cambodia as full members of the grouping but did not give a date for when they might become full members. The ASEAN announcement followed reservations last year voiced by the Philippines, Thailand and Singapore on early Burmese membership in the wake of renewed crackdowns on Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi's opposition party.

European countries and the United States have proposed sanctions against Burma and diplomats say Burma's admission as a full member to ASEAN would be tantamount to approval of the policies of Burma's military government.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
